verdict.rationale: Dagster's own OSS deployment docs describe a self-hosted Docker setup with long-running webserver, daemon, and per-code-location containers, and the core library is published on GitHub, so the core orchestrator can be self-hosted. Some capabilities, such as alerts and the MCP server, are documented as Dagster+ features, which limits parity for a self-hosted deployment. Missing for 10: explicit open-source licensing evidence, documentation of other self-host targets (e.g. Kubernetes) beyond Docker, hands-on or independent corroboration of running self-hosted, and clarity on which features are unavailable outside Dagster+.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: A typical Dagster Docker deployment includes a several long-running containers: one for the webserver, one for the daemon, and one for each code location.
With Dagster, you declare—as Python functions—the data assets that you want to build. Dagster then helps you run your functions at the right time and keep your assets up-to-date.
Dagster+ alerts can notify you of critical events occurring in your deployment so you can catch potential issues early
